newsitem.title: UK: US stocks mixed in London, MCI tumbles.
newsitem.headline: US stocks mixed in London, MCI tumbles.

text.p: Shares in MCI Communications Corp tumbled by more than ten percent in London, enlivening an otherwise dull market in U.S. shares, dealers said.
MCI shares were quoted at $38, down $4-1/2 in London after telecommunications concern said it expected its earnings for the second half of 1997 and into 1998 to be below analysts' forecasts.

In a statement issued after Wall Street closed on Thursday, MCI, set to merge with British Telecommunications Plc, blamed the expected shortfall on delays in gaining entry into the U.S. local phone service markets.
The profit warning raised concerns that MCI's $24 billion merger with BT was unravelling, a dealer said.
"Also, it's having a knock on effect because if MCI is being hurt by not being able to get into local (telephone) markets, then AT&T is probably going to be hit too," the dealer added.
Elsewhere, shares in Chrysler Corp slipped $1/4 to $34-1/2 ahead of the release of the automaker's second quarter results.
The second quarter is expected to be a difficult one for all three U.S. automakers, as labour strikes, higher incentives and slowing sales drive down profits.
Shares in General Motors Corp were down $1/4 to $56. But shares in Ford Motor Co, generally expected to suffer least, firmed $1/8 to $41-1/2.
Other U.S. shares were narrowly mixed in London, with a slight downward bias.
Dealers were expecting the Dow to open five to seven points lower unless wholesale inflation data are out of line with market's expectations.
June wholesale inflation figures are due for release at 1230 GMT. Producer prices are expected to have held steady in June after a 0.3 percent drop in May.
By 1056 GMT, September S&P 500 futures were up 0.20 point to 921.70 on Globex, while September long bond futures were up 1/32 to 113-29. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
